docs.text: Architecture and data flow ¶ transpiler-mate-runtime resolves CWL, prepares metadata, selects processes, validates options | v cwl2mcp plugin loads the first matching Tool hint delegates input/output schema conversion to cwl2ogc constructs a generated McpTool model serializes one Tool or a process-ID mapping | v tools.json The runtime owns document loading and plugin discovery. The plugin writes JSON; the converter returns a Tool without performing file I/O. An MCP server must supply execution and protocol handling separately. Two schema boundaries ¶ schemas/hints.yaml is a Schema Salad extension of CWL. Its generated mcp_hint.py validates custom hint mappings. Imported CWL and Salad classes are reused from cwl-utils and schema-salad . The generator uses Any constructor annotations; validation occurs in fromDoc() , not in those annotations. schemas/mcp-tool.yaml defines the project's MCP Tool authoring profile. Its generated mcp_tool.py contains Pydantic models. This profile is distinct from the official protocol schema. Constructing McpTool validates model fields but does not execute the embedded JSON Schemas against arguments or results. The converter preserves the literal hint name after Salad validation because Salad's shared name predicate otherwise applies document-relative identifier expansion. Input/output schema conversion uses the pinned cwl2ogc dependency; its generated schemas are copied without a separate artifact-receipt layer. Regeneration ¶ Run the configured tasks from the repository root: task generate_mpc_hint task generate_mpc_tool task generate_schema_doc The mpc spelling is the current task name. The Tool task invokes the shared Terradue json:create_models task; the hint tasks use Schema Salad. See Taskfile.yaml . Change source schemas and regenerate rather than editing generated classes or the HTML hint reference . Verification ¶ Runtime integration tests exercise real CLI discovery and exported JSON. Assertions cover the current scalar URI/DateTime projection, metadata keys, selected-process and document exports, and deterministic serialization. The hint schema tests cover the title and nested annotation handling. Run task quality:pre-commit:run for the complete quality gate. The test environments install JSON Schema format validators so malformed URI and date-time values are rejected. The hint-generation task applies reviewed Ruff rewrites and formatting after code generation. Generated loader complexity and schema-shaped signatures have file-specific Ruff exceptions; the upstream abstract-loader registration has a narrow mypy exception. Other checks remain enabled. See the comments in pyproject.toml for these generated-code boundaries.

docs.text: Configure output and metadata keys ¶ From the repository root: transpiler-mate cwl2mcp \ --output build/tool.json \ --meta-prefix org.example/mcp \ tests/examples/eoap.cwl#main --output defaults to tools.json . Missing parent directories are created; existing files are replaced after successful conversion. JSON keys are sorted, indentation is two spaces, and the file ends with a newline. --meta-prefix defaults to io.github.transpiler-mate/cwl2mcp , users can customize it keeping in mind MCP’s _meta naming rules distinguish two parts: Part Rules Optional prefix, before / Dot-separated labels; reverse DNS is recommended. Labels start with a letter, end with a letter or digit, and may contain internal hyphens. Name, after / May contain alphanumerics, hyphens, underscores, and dots. A nonempty name must start and end with an alphanumeric character. The command above produces these custom keys when their values are nonempty: org.example/mcp-aliases org.example/mcp-use-when org.example/mcp-do-not-use-when The suffixes use underscores. Empty lists and empty strings are omitted. Use tests/examples/eoap.cwl#main to export one Tool. Omit #main to export an object mapping process IDs to Tool definitions. This mapping is not an MCP tools/list response. For host integrations, construct Cwl2McpOptions(output=Path("build/tool.json"), meta_prefix="org.example/mcp") and pass it to the plugin registration's execute(context, options) method. See the API reference and crosswalk .

docs.text: Install cwl2mcp ¶ Use Python 3.10 or newer. From this repository's root, install the plugin and its runtime extra into the same environment: python -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install '.[cli]' transpiler-mate cwl2mcp --help For editable development, use python -m pip install -e '.[cli,test]' instead. Dependencies are declared in pyproject.toml ; installation normally requires network access. The package installs a plugin entry point, not a standalone cwl2mcp executable. transpiler-mate-runtime provides the transpiler-mate command. Verify the registration and the imported source: python -c "from cwl2mcp.plugin import cwl2mcp; print(cwl2mcp.name)" python -c "import cwl2mcp; print(cwl2mcp.__file__)" The first command prints cwl2mcp . If a traceback points to an older installed copy, reinstall with the interpreter belonging to that CLI environment or use an editable installation. Regenerating models in a checkout does not update a separate installation automatically. Continue with the first tool tutorial .

docs.text: Use definitions in an MCP server ¶ Generate a selected Tool using the runtime tutorial . An MCP server can then use that definition when advertising its tools. For a whole-document export, take the values of the process-ID mapping first. The plugin's JSON is not itself a protocol response. The server is responsible for listing tools, handling calls, validating arguments, executing the workflow, and returning results. See the MCP tools specification for the protocol messages and result contract. Validate incoming arguments against the generated inputSchema and returned objects against outputSchema . Enable a JSON Schema format checker if URI and date-time formats should be enforced. The generated EOAP example expects scalar URI and timestamp strings; an adapter must map them back to CWL record-shaped values if its runner requires those records. The plugin supplies no execution adapter. Tool annotations describe intended behavior and do not grant authorization. Discovery aliases in _meta do not register additional callable names. See the crosswalk for the exact exported shapes.

docs.text: Plugin and Python API ¶ Registration and options ¶ The plugin implementation registers cwl2mcp.plugin:cwl2mcp as cwl2mcp in the transpiler_mate.plugins group. The decorated object is a plugin registration; a host invokes cwl2mcp.execute(context, options) . Cwl2McpOptions rejects unknown fields: Option Python type Default output pathlib.Path tools.json meta_prefix str io.github.transpiler-mate/cwl2mcp The runtime exposes these as --output and --meta-prefix . See output configuration . When context.process_id is set, the plugin converts context.resolved_process . Otherwise it converts each process in context.document and writes a mapping keyed by the runtime's process IDs. The runtime also prepares software application metadata, but this plugin reads tool metadata from the CWL process and hint. Direct conversion ¶ from pathlib import Path from cwl_utils.parser import Process , load_document_by_uri from cwl2mcp.converter import to_mcp_tool process = load_document_by_uri ( Path ( "tests/examples/eoap.cwl" ) . resolve () . as_uri () + "#main" ) assert isinstance ( process , Process ) tool = to_mcp_tool ( process , meta_prefix = "example.org/mcp" ) payload = tool . model_dump ( by_alias = True , exclude_none = True ) to_mcp_tool(process, meta_prefix) returns the generated McpTool Pydantic model and does not write files. meta_prefix is required in the Python API. get_tool_hint(process) in converter.py returns the first matching Tool hint, or None . It accepts parsed hints and validates mapping hints using the generated Salad model. Errors ¶ Malformed hint mappings raise Schema Salad ValidationException . Invalid tool fields raise Pydantic ValidationError during conversion. Schema conversion can raise errors from cwl2ogc . The plugin wraps conversion-time ValueError as PluginFailureError . Salad validation errors are not wrapped by that handler. File-system OSError is wrapped as PluginExecutionError . Conversion finishes before the destination is opened. Parent directories are created. Writing is not an atomic replacement: an I/O failure after opening can leave a partial file. See the crosswalk for serialization details.
docs.title: Plugin and Python API

docs.text: CWL to MCP crosswalk ¶ This page describes the current converter and export plugin . The plugin generates Tool definitions; it does not execute CWL, provide an MCP server, or generate artifact receipts. Process fields ¶ CWL source Resulting JSON Current mapping Nonempty mcp:Tool.name , otherwise process id name A mapping hint's literal name is preserved. The fallback process ID is not normalized. Nonempty mcp:Tool.title , otherwise label title Omitted when neither supplies a nonempty value. Nonempty process doc description Passed directly to the model. There is no hint description override or appended guidance. inputs inputSchema Result of BaseCWLtypes2OGCConverter.get_inputs_json_schema() . outputs outputSchema Result of BaseCWLtypes2OGCConverter.get_outputs_json_schema() . mcp:Tool.annotations annotations Copies all four behavioral booleans, including false . Omitted when no hint is found. Nonempty mcp:Tool.aliases _meta["<prefix>-aliases"] Preserves the list. Nonempty mcp:Tool.useWhen _meta["<prefix>-use_when"] Preserves the string without changing description . Nonempty mcp:Tool.doNotUseWhen _meta["<prefix>-do_not_use_when"] Preserves the string without changing description . The default prefix is transpiler-mate.github.io/cwl2mcp ; configure it with --meta-prefix . The converter always supplies _meta , even when it is {} . See output configuration . The generated MCP model requires a name of 1–128 ASCII letters, digits, underscores, dots, or hyphens. A URI-valued fallback ID can therefore fail validation. Supply an explicit callable name in the hint. description must be a string; lists of CWL documentation paragraphs are not joined by the converter and can fail model validation. Hint selection and validation ¶ Only process.hints is searched. The first matching Tool is used; later matches are not rejected. requirements is not searched for MCP hints. Class names may be full URIs or use any process namespace prefix bound to https://eoap.github.io/cwl-mcp-extension# . A complete hint for the EOAP example is: hints : agent:Tool : name : inspect_source title : Inspect Source aliases : [ inspect a spatial source ] useWhen : the user needs to inspect a spatial source. doNotUseWhen : the user needs data modification. annotations : readOnlyHint : true destructiveHint : false idempotentHint : true openWorldHint : false The document must bind agent to the extension namespace. See the hint source schema and generated hint reference for field definitions. title is optional. aliases , useWhen , doNotUseWhen , annotations , and all four annotation booleans are required by the current mapping loader; empty aliases/guidance values are allowed but omitted from _meta . The schema declares name as an identifier string; Salad can synthesize a missing identifier, so an explicit MCP-compatible name should always be provided. annotations.class may be omitted. If supplied, it must identify Annotations . Tool.description is not a declared hint field and is rejected. Unknown unqualified fields and invalid field values raise validation errors. Already constructed Tool instances are returned unchanged rather than revalidated. Parameter schemas and EOAP conversion ¶ The project pins cwl2ogc in pyproject.toml . Its schemas are copied directly into the Tool; this plugin does not add parameter titles, join parameter documentation, register extra formats, or provide a custom File receipt schema. Inspect the emitted schema for the resulting types, defaults, required fields, and definitions. For the current EOAP example, the input schema contains definitions equivalent to these excerpts: { "source" : { "type" : "string" , "format" : "uri" }, "timestamp" : { "type" : "string" , "format" : "date-time" } } Properties refer to them through $ref values such as #/$defs/source . URI and DateTime records are flattened into scalar strings. The GeoJSON Point remains an object requiring type , coordinates , and bbox . Its coordinate and bounding-box values are arrays of numbers. The output schema uses corresponding source_result , timestamp_result , and point_result fields. Thus the CWL arguments fixture , which wraps URI and timestamp values in {"value": ...} , needs adaptation before it can satisfy the exported MCP input schema. See the tutorial for a matching MCP argument object. Format validation requires a format-aware JSON Schema validator. Example metadata output ¶ The EOAP example produces this metadata excerpt, alongside its input and output schemas: { "name" : "inspect_source" , "title" : "Inspect Source" , "description" : "Return a source URI, timestamp and GeoJSON point without changing their records." , "annotations" : { "readOnlyHint" : true , "destructiveHint" : false , "idempotentHint" : true , "openWorldHint" : false }, "_meta" : { "transpiler-mate.github.io/cwl2mcp-aliases" : [ "inspect a spatial source" ], "transpiler-mate.github.io/cwl2mcp-use_when" : "the user needs to inspect a spatial source." , "transpiler-mate.github.io/cwl2mcp-do_not_use_when" : "the user needs data modification." } } Export container ¶ CLI source Export tests/examples/eoap.cwl#main One MCP Tool object. tests/examples/eoap.cwl A mapping such as {"main": <Tool>} . JSON aliases are used and fields whose value is None are omitted. Keys are sorted, indentation is two spaces, and output ends with a newline. The plugin creates parent directories and completes conversion before opening the output file. It does not perform an atomic file replacement. The runtime requires software application metadata before plugin execution; the direct Python conversion API only needs a parsed process and a metadata prefix. A whole-document export is a plugin container, not an MCP tools/list response. See using definitions in MCP .
docs.title: CWL to MCP crosswalk

docs.text: Generate your first MCP Tool definition ¶ Install the plugin and runtime , then run the commands below from this repository's root. The EOAP example includes the software application metadata required by the runtime and a complete MCP hint. Its remote schema imports require network access or a populated loader cache. Export one process ¶ transpiler-mate cwl2mcp --output build/tool.json tests/examples/eoap.cwl#main python -m json.tool build/tool.json The file contains one Tool with name equal to inspect_source , title equal to Inspect Source , and inputSchema , outputSchema , annotations , and _meta . The description comes from the CWL doc ; selection guidance is in _meta . Export the document ¶ transpiler-mate cwl2mcp --output build/tools.json tests/examples/eoap.cwl This produces a mapping with a main entry containing the Tool definition. Neither command executes the expression in the CWL document. Inspect the argument contract ¶ The generated input schema accepts this shape: { "source" : "https://example.org/data.tif" , "timestamp" : "2026-10-18T06:00:00Z" , "point" : { "type" : "Point" , "coordinates" : [ 12.5 , 41.9 ], "bbox" : [ 12.5 , 41.9 , 12.5 , 41.9 ] } } The source CWL arguments fixture uses {"value": ...} records for URI and DateTime. Those wrappers are flattened by the current schema converter, so that fixture is not a valid MCP argument object without adaptation. The output schema similarly uses scalar source_result and timestamp_result fields and a structured point_result field. Read the crosswalk for current mappings, or configure the destination and metadata prefix .

docs.text: Install the plugin and runtime , then run the commands below from this repository's root. The EOAP example includes the software application metadata required by the runtime and a complete MCP hint. Its remote schema imports require network access or a populated loader cache.
docs.title: Generate your first MCP Tool definition

docs.text: transpiler-mate cwl2mcp --output build/tool.json tests/examples/eoap.cwl#main python -m json.tool build/tool.json The file contains one Tool with name equal to inspect_source , title equal to Inspect Source , and inputSchema , outputSchema , annotations , and _meta . The description comes from the CWL doc ; selection guidance is in _meta .
